1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for PVC sandal manufactured by injection moulding process.

4.3.3 The PVC sandals shall be produced in such a way to make them free from shrinkage, burning, warping and cold flow marks. 4.4 Dimension 4.4.1 The thickness of sole excluding the thickness of ribs introduced for design purpose and/or reinforcement, shall not be less than 5 mm. The thickness in the upper part of the sandal shall not be less than 2 mm. 4.4.2 PVC sandals shall have no sharp corners. 2 mm shall be maintained. 5. SAMPLING AND CRITERIA A minimum radius of

FOR CONFORMITY

5.1 The scale of sampling and criteria for conformity of the sandals to the specification shall be as prescribed in Appendix B. 6. MARKING 6.1 The sole of each sandal shall bear the name of the manufacturer or his trade-mark, if any; it shall also be marked with the corresponding English size. 6.1.1 The marking as stated in 6.1 shall be incorporated in the moulds. Marking by indelible ink or otherwise shall not be permitted. 6.1.2 Mark. The sandals may also be marked with the IS1 Certification

NOTE - The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. ISI marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that Details of conditions under which a licence for the standard as a further safeguard. use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

*

7. PACKING 7.1 The sandals shall be suitably packed in pairs as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 8. TEST METHODS 8.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, all tests shall be carried out within three months from the date of receipt of the material by the purchaser. 8.2 Test pieces for relative density and hardness shall be prepared directly from the representative sample selected in accordance with 5.1. 5

IS : 6721.1972 8.2.1 For all other tests, test slabs made of the same composition as that of the material used for making sandals and cured under identical conditions shall be supplied by the supplier.
NOTE -The supplier shall issue certif;cate to the effect that these slabs are made with the same composition and cured under identical condition.

IS : 6721- 1972 G-1.3 Test Method

A-1.3.1 Pre,baralion and Conditioning of Test Piece-The test piece shall have a surface, free from crevices as far as possible, weighing at 5 g. The test piece shall then be conditioned to a moisture equilibrium in an atm&phere of 65 f 2 percent relative humidity and temperature 27 f 2�C (S&e iS : I96-1966* ) for 24 hours prior to testing. A-l.4 ProcedureSuspend the test piece from the hook on one side of the balance using a suitable length of wire, so that the bottom of the teat piece does not touch the bottom of the beaker and weigh. Counter balance the wire previously by a length of wire on the other pan. Repeat the weighing with the test piece completely immersed in the freshly boiled and cooled distilled water to a temperature of 27 f 2"C, in a beaker. Allow sufficient time for the test piece to attain the temperature of the Make sure that there are no air bubbles on the surface of the water. specimen and the wire while immersed in water. IS: 6721.1972 A-3.5.2 Insert a dumb-bell test piece into the grips of the tensile testing machine taking care to adjust it symmetrically so that the tension will be If tension is greater on one distributed uniformly over the cross-section. side of the test piece than the other, the reference lines will not remain parallel and the maximum strength of the piece will not be developed. A-3.6 Calculation tensile strength by dividing the A-3.6.1 Tensile Strength -Calculate load at break by the initial area of cross-section of the test piece. Express the result in kg/cm2 and report the medium of three results excluding the results on any dumb-bell test piece which breaks outside the reference lines. A-3.6.2 Elongation at BreakCalculate elongation at break by subtracting the initial distance between the reference lines on the dumb-bell test piece from the distance between the lines at breaking point and expressing the results as a percentage of the initial distance. Report the medium of three results excluding the result on any dumb-bell test piece which breaks outside the reference line. A-4. A-4.1.2 Micrometer Dial Gauge - Th e instrument for measuring the thickness of tear test pieces shall consist of a micrometer dial gauge firmly held in a rigid stand over a flat base-plate of diameter at least 50 mm. The The gauge shall have a scale graduated in. unit divisions of 0.01 mm. dial gauge shall be fitted with a flat contact, square to the plunger and parallel to the base plate, and shall operate with a pressure of 0.2 f 0.03 bar. NOTE-It is preferable for the gauge to have a contact area of diameter about 4 mm as this may be used on almost all test pieces without any subpart of the contact
area over-hanging the test piece edge, which would increase the contact pressure.

A-4.1.3 Measuring Instrument - For measuring the depth of the nick, an optical instrument shall be used, the test piece being mounted so that the nick is slightly opened in order to make it visible.
A-4.1.3.1 When it is only necessary to check that the depth of the nick is within the specified limits, any suitable means may be used, for example, A convenient arrangement is a microan optical projection apparatus. scope giving about 100 x magnification and fitted with travelling stage The eye-piece is fitted with a graticule to record suitably illuminated. the travel of the stage and test piece through a distance equal to the depth of the nick. The travel of the stage is calibrated with a stage micrometer graticule. A-4.1.3.2 Alternatively, a travelling microscope may apparatus shall show an accuracy of at least 0.025 mm. be used. The

A-4.1.4 Tensile resting Machine-The tensile testing machine shall be power driven and of such capacity that the maximum force required for the test is not greater than 85 percent nor less than 15 percent of the maximum of the scale. The rate of traverse of the driven grip shall he 500 f 50 mm per minute and the power shall be sufficient to maintain the rate substantially constant up to the maximum capacity of the machine. 10

IS : 6721:1972 The machine shall be equipped to give a stretching of the test piece. After the test piece is broken, the indicators shall remain at the point of maximum force. The machine shall be provided with a type of grip which tightens automatically as the tension increases and exerts a uniform pressure across the widened end of the test piece. Each grip shall incorporate a positioning device so that all test pieces are inserted to a depth of 15 to 20 mm and are in axial alignment with the direction of pull.
NATE - The force scale shall be calibrated by a suitable method at least every six month to ensure that the error does not exceed 1.5 percent of the applied force or 0.3 percent of the maximum of the scale whichever is greater.

A-4.2

Test Piece

A-4.2.1 The test piece of the dimensions as shown in Fig. 1, shall be cut from the sheet by punching with a die using a single stroke of a press where the cut edge shall be normal to the surface. The thickness of the test piece shall be 2.0 f 0.2 mm and shall be measured by means of a micrometer gauge specified in A-4.1.2. The thickness in the region of the test area shall nowhere deviate by morz than f 2 percent from the mean. A-4.2.2 A single nick or slit of O-50 f 0.08 mm shall be cut with extreme care and accuracy, symmetrically across the centre of the concave inner edge of the test piece. Test pieces falling out of the tolerance specified for the nick shall be discarded. A-4.3 Procedure at least three, preferably six test pieces. Apparatus JNessler Cylinder 50 ml capacity.

A-6.1.1 A-6.2

Reagents 0.29 of p-nitrophenol

A-6.2.1 P-Nitrophenol Indicator Solution -Dissolve in hot water and dilute to 100 ml. A-6.2.2 A-6.2.3 A-6.2.4 Dilute Ammonium HydroxideDilute Hydrochloric Acid1 : 9.

1 : 99. and freshly prepared.

Hydrogen Sulghide Solution -saturated

A-6.2.5 Standard Lead Solution - Dissolve 1.60 g of lead nitrate in water and make up the solution to 1000 ml with water. Pipette out 10 ml of the solution and'dilute again to 1000 ml with water. One millilitre of this solution contains O-0 1 mg of lead (as Pb). A-6.3 ProcedureWeigh accurately 5 g of the material and thoroughly shake it with 25 ml of water for 5 minutes and filter. Take the filterate in a Nessler cylinder and add one drop of p-nitrophenol indicator solution. Add dilute ammonium hydroxide dropwise until the solution turns yellow. Add dilute hydrochloric acid dropwise until the solution becomes colourless and then add O-5 ml of the acid in excess. Add 5 ml of hydrogen sulphide solution, dilute to the mark and mix well. Carry out a control test in a similar manner in another Nessler cylinder using 1 ml of standard lead solution taken as not having been exceeded if the intensity of colour produced with the material is not greater than produced in the control test. 13
